name: DotGrid-TS-TW

frames.best_why: Dots are shoved open in a wide ring around the cursor, with cyan dots glowing, the most visible ripple.

tagline: A field of violet dots that scatters and lights up cyan around the cursor.
summary: A full-bleed canvas draws an even grid of round violet dots. Moving the pointer tints nearby dots toward cyan, and fast swipes or clicks knock dots out of place so they spring back.
appearance: A near-black stage covered edge to edge in a regular lattice of small violet circles, evenly spaced with wide gaps. The dots are flat single-colour discs, denser than a typical starfield.
behaviour: At rest the lattice is even. As the pointer moves, dots within reach blend toward bright cyan, and a fast swipe pushes the nearest ones away; they drift back with an elastic spring. A click sends a circular shockwave of displacement outward.
search_phrases: interactive dots that follow the mouse
particle grid background for a hero
violet dots that glow near pointer
use_when: You want a full-page backdrop that reacts to the pointer without stealing attention from the text above it.
avoid_when: Touch-only layouts or low-power devices: the effect is pointer-driven and redraws every frame.
customise: Dot size, spacing, both colours, reaction radius, swipe threshold and shock strength are props. The spring feel lives in the GSAP calls and needs a source edit.
weight_why: A canvas repaints every dot on every animation frame for the whole session.

a11y.note: Purely pointer-driven decoration: nothing to focus, no keyboard path, and no reduced-motion check to stop the loop.

polish_why: Even spacing and a convincing spring; the dot colour is faint against the black stage.
